Inter-unit reliability of a provider measure

Source: R/reliability_iur.R
iur.Rd

The fraction of the variation of a provider-level measure that reflects true differences between providers rather than within-provider sampling noise, \(\mathrm{IUR} = \sigma^2_b / (\sigma^2_b + \sigma^2_w / n')\), from an ANOVA-type decomposition of the measure's variance (He et al. 2019). Three estimators, chosen by method:

  • "direct" uses provider-level estimates and their standard errors (for instance a standardized rate and the se_rate of standardize());

  • "bootstrap" resamples the rows of every provider with replacement and takes the variance of the resampled measures as the within-provider variance;

  • "split_half" splits every provider's rows into two random halves and converts the agreement of the two halves' measures across providers into a reliability by the Spearman-Brown formula \(2r / (1 + r)\); six agreement coefficients are reported (weighted kappa, Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho of the measures cut into ordered categories, and Pearson's r, Kendall's tau and Spearman's rho of the measures themselves).

Usage

iur(
  method = c("direct", "bootstrap", "split_half"),
  estimate = NULL,
  se = NULL,
  size = NULL,
  obs = NULL,
  expected = NULL,
  provider = NULL,
  n_boot = 100,
  n_iter = 10,
  category_probs = c(0.1, 0.3, 0.7, 0.9),
  measure = NULL,
  seed = NULL
)

ratio_measure(obs, expected, provider)

Arguments

method

"direct", "bootstrap" or "split_half".

estimate, se

provider-level estimates and standard errors (direct method).

size

number of observations per provider.

obs, expected

observed and expected outcome per row (patient; bootstrap and split-half methods).

provider

provider identifier per row.

n_boot

number of bootstrap replicates. Default 100.

n_iter

number of random splits. Default 10.

category_probs

quantile probabilities that cut the measures into ordered categories for the categorical coefficients.

measure

a function (obs, expected, provider) returning one value per provider in sorted provider order; by default the ratio of sums \(\sum O / \sum E\).

seed

optional seed; the session's random-number state is restored afterwards.

Value

An object of class pp_iur: a list with method, iur (for the split-half method a named vector of the six coefficients' reliabilities), and for the direct and bootstrap methods s2_between, s2_within, n_prime, n_providers, providers, sizes, measure, iur_providers (each provider's reliability at its own size) and, for the bootstrap, the replicates matrix; for the split-half method iterations (one row per split) and excluded (providers with fewer than two rows).

Details

With sizes \(n_i\), within variances \(v_i\) of the provider-level measure and measures \(T_i\): the pooled within variance \(s^2_{w} = \sum (n_i - 1) v_i / \sum (n_i - 1)\), the effective size \(n' = (N - \sum n_i^2 / N) / (m - 1)\), the total variance \(s^2_t = \sum n_i (T_i - \bar T)^2 / (n'(m - 1))\) with \(\bar T\) the size-weighted mean, the between variance \(s^2_b = s^2_t - s^2_w\), and \(\mathrm{IUR} = s^2_b / s^2_t\). The reported s2_within is \(n' s^2_w\), the record-level within variance, so that the reliability of a provider of size \(n\) is \(s^2_b / (s^2_b + s2\_within / n)\) (see iur_curve()).

References

He K, Kalbfleisch JD, Yang Y, Li Y (2019). Inter-unit reliability for nonlinear models. Statistics in Medicine, 38(5), 844-854.

See also

iur_curve(), iur_stratified()

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 30, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
fit <- fit_logistic_fe(pd)
expected <- stats::median(coef(fit)$gamma) + fit$linear_predictor
expected <- stats::plogis(expected)
boot <- iur("bootstrap", obs = fit$data$y, expected = expected,
            provider = fit$data$provider, n_boot = 50, seed = 1)
boot
#> Bootstrap inter-unit reliability: 0.8444 (30 providers)
#>   between variance 0.101, within variance 2.682, effective size 144.1
iur_curve(boot)
#>     size_group      size       iur
#> 1          min  51.00000 0.6575734
#> 2   quantile 1  61.66667 0.6989740
#> 3   quantile 2  80.66667 0.7523153
#> 4   quantile 3 108.75000 0.8037226
#> 5   quantile 4 114.00000 0.8110538
#> 6   quantile 5 128.66667 0.8289067
#> 7   quantile 6 159.33333 0.8571321
#> 8   quantile 7 168.66667 0.8639624
#> 9   quantile 8 198.66667 0.8820827
#> 10  quantile 9 208.00000 0.8867747
#> 11 quantile 10 221.00000 0.8927205
#> 12         max 231.00000 0.8968858
